      worked_attack:

        part_1_exact_sequence_rederivation: >-
          Re-derived by hand, from the statement of the sequence alone
          (per attack_plan, "not the producer's chain"). Given: E/Q,
          E(Q)_tors = {O} (trivial), rank(E) >= 31 already certified via 31
          exhibited independent points, and the exact sequence
          0 -> E(Q)/2E(Q) -> Sel_2(E) -> Sha(E)[2] -> 0 (exact, unconditional,
          textbook). By Mordell-Weil (unconditional theorem), E(Q) is
          finitely generated; with trivial torsion, E(Q) ~= Z^rank(E), so
          E(Q)/2E(Q) ~= (Z/2Z)^rank(E) and dim_F2(E(Q)/2E(Q)) = rank(E)
          exactly -- no hypothesis beyond trivial torsion and Mordell-Weil is
          used here. Exactness of the sequence gives
          dim Sel_2(E) = dim(E(Q)/2E(Q)) + dim Sha(E)[2]
                       = rank(E) + dim Sha(E)[2],
          and since dim Sha(E)[2] >= 0 always (it is the dimension of an
          F2-vector space, never negative), rank(E) <= dim Sel_2(E)
          unconditionally, with no conjecture (no BSD, no GRH, no finiteness
          of Sha) anywhere in this step. If dim Sel_2(E) = 31 exactly: since
          rank(E) >= 31 (already certified) and rank(E) <= dim Sel_2(E) = 31,
          rank(E) = 31 is FORCED, and moreover dim Sha(E)[2] = 0 is a
          CONSEQUENCE of this squeeze, not an assumption fed into it. This
          matches protocol.yaml's READING (a) (lines 287-292) exactly and is
          mathematically sound and fully unconditional as stated.
          If dim Sel_2(E) >= 32: rank(E) = dim Sel_2(E) - dim Sha(E)[2] could
          still equal 31 if dim Sha(E)[2] >= dim Sel_2(E) - 31 >= 1, so a
          32nd independent point is licensed but not guaranteed -- matches
          READING (b) (lines 293-301) and is correctly, honestly hedged (no
          overclaim of guarantee). CONCUR on this abstract implication: it is
          the correct, unconditional consequence of the exact sequence given
          trivial torsion and the certified rank >= 31 floor.

        part_2_enumeration_exhaustiveness_attack__THE_BREAK: >-
          Attack-plan item (a) asks whether "the enumeration over 2^|S_L|
          classes [is] genuinely exhaustive, or does it test a subgroup".
          protocol.yaml states, at search_boundary.stage_a_selmer_computation
          (lines 899-930) and again at claim (line 279) and object_first
          (lines 205-210) and target_complexity (lines 752-753): S = {2}
          union {primes dividing Delta(E)}, and enumeration_order (line
          916-930) literally specifies: "Index each of the 2^|S_L| classes
          of L(S,2), where S_L is that set of primes of L [above S], by the
          bit-vector of exponents (0 or 1) over S_L in that fixed order" --
          i.e. the protocol treats L(S,2) as IN BIJECTION with subsets of
          S_L, dimension exactly |S_L|, generated purely by the primes of L
          above S.
          This is FALSE for L(S,2) as actually defined (the group of square
          classes in L*/(L*)^2 whose divisor is supported on primes above S,
          i.e. the S-unit group O_{L,S}^* mod squares). By the S-unit
          theorem, dim_F2(O_{L,S}^*/(O_{L,S}^*)^2) = |S_L| + rank(O_L^*) + e
          for a small torsion term e in {0,1}, where rank(O_L^*) is the
          ORDINARY (non-S) unit rank of L given by Dirichlet's unit theorem:
          rank(O_L^*) = r1 + r2 - 1, where r1, r2 are L's real and complex
          places. L is here the cubic resolvent field (degree 3 over Q,
          since torsion:[] in the frozen JSON forces the resolvent cubic to
          be irreducible -- protocol.yaml's own
          rational_2_torsion_applicability control at lines 1079-1081 notes
          this). For a degree-3 field, r1 + 2*r2 = 3, so (r1,r2) is either
          (3,0) [totally real, unit rank 2] or (1,1) [one real place, one
          complex pair, unit rank 1]. EITHER WAY rank(O_L^*) >= 1, strictly
          positive -- there is no cubic field with unit rank 0 (that would
          require r1+r2=1, impossible given r1+2r2=3 with r1,r2 >= 0
          integers). Therefore dim_F2 L(S,2) = |S_L| + rank(O_L^*) + e >
          |S_L| by at least 1, in every case, regardless of the class number
          of L.
          This is exactly why full 2-descent via the cubic resolvent is
          fundamentally harder than descent via a rational 2-isogeny: the
          latter's ambient group Q(S,2) is a bitvector space over S alone
          PRECISELY BECAUSE Q has unit rank 0 (Dirichlet: r1+r2-1 = 1+0-1 =
          0 for Q), so "|S| bits, no more" is valid ONLY in that degenerate
          case. protocol.yaml itself correctly distinguishes L(S,2) from
          Q(S,2) at the tracked_object level (line ~906-909: "NOT the
          squarefree-integer space Q(S,2)... inapplicable here"), but its
          concrete enumeration_order procedure (lines 916-930) then silently
          reverts to describing exactly the Q(S,2)-style construction (pure
          bitvectors over a prime list) applied to L(S,2), omitting the
          unit-group generators of O_L^* entirely, and omitting any
          treatment of Cl(L)[2] (needed when h(L) is even, to correct for
          primes of S_L that are not principal).
          Consequence for the decision gate: a literal implementation of
          enumeration_order as written enumerates a PROPER SUBGROUP of the
          true L(S,2) -- it never constructs or tests any class that
          requires a nontrivial unit-group component. Any genuine Selmer
          class (an element of the true Sel_2(E) subset of L(S,2)) whose
          representative is not expressible purely as a product of the
          chosen S_L-prime generators would never be generated, hence never
          tested for local solubility, hence silently absent from the
          reported count. A run of this literal procedure reporting
          "dim Sel_2(E) = 31" therefore establishes only that 31 classes
          WITHIN THE INCOMPLETE TESTED SUBSPACE pass local solubility -- it
          does not establish that the TRUE dim Sel_2(E) (computed over the
          full L(S,2)) equals 31. The true dim Sel_2(E) could be strictly
          larger, hiding room for a genuine 32nd independent point that this
          procedure, as specified, structurally cannot detect. This is a
          concrete instance of review-plan.yaml's own predicted breaking
          pattern: "a class ... survives outside the enumerated space" (the
          missing unit-group-derived classes are exactly such a class),
          "silently turning 'dim = 31' into a non-decisive lower bound" on
          the TESTED subspace rather than an exact value of Sel_2(E) itself.
          Note this is not a mere cost/completeness caveat (already disclosed
          honestly elsewhere as a budget-ceiling risk in
          budgets_and_stops.stage_a_selmer_computation, lines 1140-1179): a
          budget ceiling that halts early is reported as "undetermined
          within budget" (correct, per AGENTS.md rule 3/5). This is
          different and worse: the enumeration_order procedure, even if run
          to COMPLETION against its own stated 2^|S_L| bound with unlimited
          budget, still could not reach the true dim Sel_2(E), because its
          ambient candidate space is the wrong (too small) group by
          construction, not merely budget-truncated within the right group.

        part_3_decision_gate_arithmetic_phrasing_minor_note: >-
          Attack-plan item (b) asks whether the decision gate's "equal to
          E(Q)_tors[2]=0 plus the already-certified 31" arithmetic (line 944)
          is right given trivial torsion. Read literally as "31 = 0 + 31" it
          is not false, but it is an imprecise/incomplete gloss: the actual
          unconditional justification (part_1 above) is dim Sel_2(E) =
          rank(E) + dim Sha(E)[2] with dim Sha(E)[2] >= 0 forcing the squeeze
          -- Sha(E)[2] is never named at the decision_gate itself, only in
          the separate `mechanism` block (lines ~302-309). This is a
          documentation-clarity gap, not a mathematical error, and is NOT
          counted as part of the breaking_artifact for this verdict; noted
          for completeness since attack-plan item (b) explicitly asked for
          it to be checked.

        part_4_conjecture_dependency_check: >-
          Attack-plan item (c): named dependency set. READING (a) as derived
          in part_1 requires only Mordell-Weil finite generation (theorem)
          and exactness of the 2-descent sequence (theorem) -- CONFIRMED
          fully unconditional, no BSD/GRH/Sha-finiteness needed, consistent
          with protocol.yaml's own claim. READING (b) is correctly stated as
          licensed-not-guaranteed (Sha(E)[2] possibly nonzero is disclosed,
          lines 293-301 and interpretation_limits lines 685-693) -- CONFIRMED
          not overclaimed as unconditional. No issue found in this sub-item.

      breaking_artifact: >-
        protocol.yaml's search_boundary.stage_a_selmer_computation.enumeration_order
        (lines 916-930), and its restatements of the prime-set/enumeration
        size at lines 205-210, 279-280, 752-753, and 910-912, describe L(S,2)
        as generated solely by bit-vectors over S_L (the primes of the cubic
        resolvent field L above S), with dimension exactly |S_L|. This omits
        the unit-group contribution rank(O_L^*) = r1+r2-1 >= 1 (Dirichlet's
        unit theorem, forced positive for any degree-3 field since r1+2r2=3
        admits no solution with r1+r2 <= 1) and any class-group correction.
        The enumeration as literally specified therefore tests a proper
        subgroup of the true L(S,2), not the ambient space Sel_2(E) actually
        lives in. A reported "dim Sel_2(E) = 31" from this procedure would
        not be the exact quantity the decision gate (line 943-949) requires
        to invoke unconditional closure -- it would be the dimension of a
        strictly smaller tested space, and the true dim Sel_2(E) could
        exceed it, leaving room for an undetected 32nd independent point.

      recommended_fix_note: >-
        Not prescriptive (out of scope for this review), but for the
        Coordinator's use: any second full-2-descent-via-cubic-resolvent
        write-up that fixes enumeration_order would need to specify how the
        S-unit group O_{L,S}^*/(O_{L,S}^*)^2 is actually computed (a
        nontrivial number-field computation requiring the unit group and, if
        h(L) > 1, class-group data of L, not merely a sorted prime list) --
        this is a genuine implementation-complexity increase, not a cosmetic
        fix, and materially changes the Stage A cost model in
        budgets_and_stops (lines 1140-1179), which currently costs only the
        S_L bitvector space.

    - joint: J4
      title: Baseline reproduction specification fidelity
      verdict: DISSENT
      scope_note: >-
        Per attack_plan: check every protocol-quoted constant verbatim
        against the frozen JSON; check the short-Weierstrass conversion's
        stated role is coherent; check the torsion-determination method is
        stated at a strength that proves E(Q)_tors = {O} exactly, not merely
        |E(F_p)| constraints. Most checks CONCUR; one derived (not directly
        quoted) constant is verifiably wrong against the correctly-quoted
        source data, which is sufficient for DISSENT on fidelity.

      worked_attack:

        verbatim_constant_checks_PASS: >-
          Checked digit-for-digit against
          coordination/goals/GOAL-ECQ-e72c0b/baseline/icarm_curve_302_20260824.json.
          ainvs (a1,a2,a3,a4,a6): protocol.yaml quotes
          ("1","1","1","-1284727764113567728281797636015784768866707681415849262157224232063",
          "560368321454261339256859338901915312332769858684945406858043869199456710681989058863306170127006181"),
          matching JSON `ainvs` field exactly, entry for entry. Discriminant:
          protocol.yaml's 204-digit string (lines ~274-276) matches JSON
          `discriminant` (line 38) character-for-character on manual
          segment-by-segment comparison (compared in 10-digit chunks; no
          discrepancy found). rank_lower_bound: JSON value 31 matches every
          protocol.yaml reference to "31 exhibited/certified points". torsion:
          JSON `torsion: []` (trivial) matches protocol.yaml's repeated
          "E(Q)_tors trivial" / "E(Q)_tors[2] = 0" claims. Spot-checked two
          rational-denominator example points explicitly quoted in
          protocol.yaml's baseline_reproduction.on_curve_checks (line
          ~829-831): x = 8050101189939018648004785213625795/9 matches JSON
          `points` entry (JSON line 102) verbatim; x =
          -11477003798992551861310315487329257523535/8922169 matches JSON
          `points` entry (JSON line 162, the final point) verbatim. All 31
          `points` array entries were counted in the JSON (lines 41-164, 31
          bracketed [x,y] pairs) and match protocol.yaml's stated count of
          31.

        prime_set_construction_check__THE_BREAK: >-
          protocol.yaml repeatedly derives, from the frozen JSON's
          `bad_primes` list, the claim "|S| <= 21 (20 listed bad primes plus
          2)" -- at lines 205-210 ("|S| is bounded by the 20 listed bad
          primes... plus 2"), line 279-280 ("at most 21 primes -- 20 listed
          bad primes plus 2"), lines 752-753 ("|S| <= 21 (20 bad primes plus
          2)"), and lines 910-912 ("S = {2} union {primes dividing
          Delta(E)}... |S| <= 21 (20 listed bad primes plus 2"). This treats
          "2" as an ADDITIONAL element beyond the 20 listed bad primes.
          Checked against the frozen JSON's `bad_primes` array (JSON lines
          16-37): it contains exactly 20 entries, and the FIRST entry (JSON
          line 17) is "2" itself -- curve 302 already has bad reduction at
          2. Therefore S = {2} union {primes dividing Delta(E)} = bad_primes
          exactly, as a SET, with |S| = 20, not 21: the protocol's own
          declared construction double-counts the prime 2 (once via the
          explicit "{2}" term, once via bad_primes[0] = "2"). Numerically
          the stated bound "|S| <= 21" is not violated (20 <= 21 remains
          true), but it is not the actual value the protocol's own
          correctly-quoted source data yields, and the error propagates: the
          |S_L| <= 3|S| <= 63 bound at lines 210, 753, and 1143 should read
          <= 60 under the correct |S| = 20, and the enumeration_order
          instruction to "sort S in ascending numeric order" (line 917) is
          ambiguous about whether S is built as a genuine set (2 appears
          once) or as a literal union/concatenation of the singleton {2}
          with the bad_primes list (2 could appear twice, corrupting the
          canonical-order sort and the induced "primes of L above S" step by
          processing 2's splitting behavior in L twice). This is exactly the
          class of check attack-plan item asks for under "prime-set
          guidance": a protocol-derived constant that does not follow from
          the frozen record it claims to derive from.

        short_weierstrass_identity_check_PASS: >-
          Verified by symbolic inspection (no computation, pure algebraic
          identity check): for E: y^2 = x^3 + Ax + B (short Weierstrass),
          the standard discriminant is Delta_E = -16(4A^3 + 27B^2)
          (Silverman AEC III.1). The resolvent cubic here is x^3 + Ax + B
          itself (its roots are the 2-torsion x-coordinates), with
          disc(x^3+Ax+B) = -4A^3 - 27B^2 by the standard cubic-discriminant
          formula. Then 16*disc(resolvent cubic) = 16*(-4A^3-27B^2) =
          -16(4A^3+27B^2) = Delta_E exactly. protocol.yaml's claimed identity
          "Delta_E = 16*disc(resolvent cubic)" (used at lines ~205-210 and
          in baseline_reproduction.short_weierstrass_conversion.why_needed)
          is CORRECT for a curve already in short Weierstrass form.
          protocol.yaml correctly flags (confounders, lines ~663-670) that
          curve 302 is NOT given in short form (a1=a2=a3=1, all nonzero per
          the frozen JSON) and that the conversion must be re-derived at
          Stage 0 before this identity is used to fix S -- this caveat is
          appropriately conservative and not a break.

        torsion_determination_strength_check_PASS: >-
          protocol.yaml's torsion_determination method (gcd of #E(F_p) over
          >= 2 good odd primes, citing injectivity of reduction on
          prime-to-p torsion at good primes p, Silverman AEC VII.3.1) is
          stated at the correct strength: reduction mod a good ODD prime p
          is injective on the prime-to-p part of E(Q)_tors, so if
          gcd(#E(F_p1), #E(F_p2), ...) = 1 over several distinct good odd
          primes, no prime can divide every #E(F_pi), forcing E(Q)_tors =
          {O} exactly and unconditionally -- this is a genuine proof of
          triviality, not merely a divisibility constraint on
          #E(F_p) individually. This matches the frozen JSON's torsion: []
          and is not merely restating |E(F_p)| bounds. No issue found.

        sha256_check_NOT_VERIFIABLE_under_zero_execution: >-
          protocol.yaml's header_note (line ~16-18) and claim block (line
          ~277) both cite "sha256 2bd422f34d0566f79c53f6bc94c6ec5f9ff048cd88fcc300f53e0b397af2e67b"
          for the frozen baseline JSON file. This hash is not itself a field
          inside the JSON and cannot be independently confirmed by hand
          derivation -- computing a SHA-256 digest requires execution (the
          HARD RULE 1 zero-execution constraint on this review explicitly
          forbids command execution and computer algebra). This is
          DISCLOSED as unverified by this review, neither confirmed nor
          contradicted; it is not counted toward this verdict either way.

      breaking_artifact: >-
        protocol.yaml's repeated derived claim "|S| <= 21 (20 listed bad
        primes plus 2)" (lines 205-210, 279-280, 752-753, 910-912) does not
        follow from the frozen JSON's own bad_primes array (JSON lines
        16-37), whose first entry is already "2" (curve 302 has bad
        reduction at 2). The correct value is |S| = 20 exactly, since S =

        actually follows from the correctly-quoted frozen source data,
        propagating into the |S_L| <= 3|S| <= 63 cost bound (should read

        literal "S = {2} union {primes dividing Delta(E)}" construction

      severity_note: >-

        stated upper bound is not itself violated, and every other
        verbatim-quoted baseline constant checked (ainvs, discriminant,

        determination method's strength) CONCURS with the frozen record.
        DISSENT is issued because the joint's own charge is fidelity of the
        baseline-reproduction specification against the frozen record, and
        this is a genuine, checkable failure of that fidelity on the
        prime-set derivation specifically named in the attack plan, not a
        judgment call.

  summary_for_coordinator: >-
